dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you! It's been a while!

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: How have what things been... Oh, you mean my work here?

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Well, we've been dealing with various issues for people whose livelihoods have been affected by the war... I doubt you'd be enthused to hear about such dry stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Nonetheless, I'm doing pretty alright. Thanks for your concern.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about that whole Enkanomiya business...

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Her Excellency the Divine Priestess has yet to authorize our request to open Enkanomiya. We'll just have to wait for her to make the call.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: In any case, our primary task right now is the restoration of the peoples' lives... More long term plans will have to wait for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Still, I can't say I'm not excited to find out what our ancestral lands deep beneath the ocean waves looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: In any case, the conclusion of this matter was thanks to your help as well. Allow me to express our gratitude once again.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: See you. Watatsumi Island will always welcome you.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: Enkanomiya's name was Byakuyakoku once upon a time. There was neither sun nor moon in that underground realm, and the only two astronomical phenomena being the Whitenight and the Evernight.

dialogues.speaker: Tsuyuko
dialogues.text: One of my ancestors was a shrine maiden named Eboshi. She was a character of some significance in Byakuyakoku's history, and it is due to her that I am in charge of the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri.
